guide.summary: Museums, a historic stadium, tavernas, fine dining, cocktail bars, cafés and sweet shops in Athens, each checked against its own website.
guide.tip: Several museums shut on Tuesdays, including the Museum of Cycladic Art, the Byzantine and Christian Museum and the Jewish Museum's venues, while the National Archaeological Museum opens only at 13:00 that day.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Museum of Cycladic Art and the Byzantine and Christian Museum close on Tuesdays, and the Jewish Museum's listed venues are closed Tuesdays too. The National Archaeological Museum opens on Tuesday only from 13:00 to 20:00.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: The National Archaeological Museum sells its 20€ admission through the e-ticketing system, and the Acropolis Museum and Goulandris Museum link to online tickets. The Panathenaic Stadium charges 12 euros, with a 30-minute audio guide included.

toolkit.label: Booking
toolkit.copy: Spondi, Varoulko Seaside, Cookoovaya, Hytra and both Karamanlidika branches take online reservations. The Clumsies says reservations by website or phone get an immediate response.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: The Panathenaic Stadium allows no food or drinks other than water, and only certified service animals. At the Museum of Cycladic Art, children under 18 enter free and last entry is 15 minutes before closing.

guide.dek: Plan museum days around Tuesday closures and book dinner tables online ahead.
intro: Athens rewards you for planning around museum hours. The Acropolis Museum on Dionysiou Areopagitou is showing "The Parthenon and Byron" until 31 December 2026, and it runs a family programme from 1 November 2026 to 28 March 2027. Across town, the National Archaeological Museum on Patission opens Wednesday to Monday from 08:00 to 20:00 until 15 November 2026, with a later 13:00 start on Tuesdays. Its exhibition "Pylos of Nestor: A Mycenaean Kingdom Revealed" runs to 31 January 2027, and William Kentridge's "Imitate the sleep of stones" opens 30 October 2026.

Along Vasilissis Sofias you can pair two museums in one walk. The Museum of Cycladic Art opens 10:00 to 17:00 most days, stays open until 20:00 on Thursdays and closes on Tuesdays, while visitors currently enter through the Stathatos Mansion because the other entrance is under construction. The Byzantine and Christian Museum nearby opens 8:30 to 15:30 and also closes on Tuesdays. The Goulandris Museum on Eratosthenous opens "BELLE ÉPOQUE" on 31 October 2026, running to 15 February 2027, and EMST shows a Niki Kanagini retrospective until 14 February 2027.

For something open daily, the Panathenaic Stadium welcomes you from 8:00 to 19:00 through October and 8:00 to 17:00 from November to February. A general ticket costs 12 euros and includes a 30-minute audio guide, and only water is allowed inside. The Jewish Museum of Greece's exhibition "Like Hunted Birds" runs at the Bathhouse of the Winds in Plaka until 30 November 2026, daily except Tuesday, and the Ilias Lalaounis Jewelry Museum below the Acropolis plans a free art fair on 5 and 6 December.

Eating and drinking are easy to book ahead. Varoulko Seaside in Piraeus and Cookoovaya both serve daily from 13:00 to midnight and take online bookings, and Spondi and Hytra also reserve online. Klimataria on Platia Theatrou opens from noon to 2am with live music most evenings. For coffee, Mokka on Athinas has roasted in the same building since 1923. Baba au Rum pours from 19:00 to 03:00, and 360 Cocktail Bar on Ifaistou opens from 10:00 for brunch and stays open late.
summaryCards: Start at the Acropolis Museum and the Panathenaic Stadium, then book a table at Karamanlidika or Cookoovaya.
Pick up coffee at Mokka on Athinas, then spend the late morning at the Museum of Cycladic Art, which opens at 10:00 except on Tuesdays.
Check Tuesday closures at the Cycladic, Byzantine and Jewish museums, and reserve Spondi, Varoulko Seaside or Hytra online.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The Acropolis archaeological site could not be confirmed because the Ministry of Culture page refused connection and hhticket.gr and culture.gov.gr returned 403; the Benaki Museum, SNFCC and the Hilton (Galaxy Bar) also returned 403, Kuzina and the Eugenides Planetarium had certificate errors, and Strofi returned HTTP 520. Several input places (Kora Bakery, Takis Bakery, Dope Roasting Co., Tailor Made, Nolan, This is Loco, Betty's Bakery, Kostas Souvlaki) had no readable official site, and the domains formerly used by Nolan and Six d.o.g.s now show gambling content. Opening hours were not published on the pages read for the Acropolis Museum, Goulandris, Spondi, Karamanlidika, Hytra, Feyrouz, Lukumades, Mokka, Little Kook, The Clumsies, Line, Brettos and A for Athens; Lalaounis hours were only partly readable. For Lukumades and Brettos, current operation rests only on a 2026 copyright notice, and Line and A for Athens on booking links without 2026 content.
